summary: The Bahamas' Department of Immigration lists 155 countries, territories and islands (as of 8 October 2026) whose citizens need no visa for stays of up to three or eight months, as each agreement dictates; the Ministry of Foreign Affairs also lists Benin and Ghana as visa-free, but Bosnia and Herzegovina as needing a visa. Citizens of countries on the visa-required lists must obtain a visa before traveling. Every visitor presents a completed Bahamas Immigration Disembarkation/Embarkation Card at the border.

fee.notes: Single-entry visitor visa, non-refundable, paid by card when you apply online. A multiple-entry visa for 3 months, 6 months or 1 year costs $250 and needs copies of three earlier Bahamas visas; a 3-year multiple-entry visa costs $500 and cannot be applied for online.

source.name: Bahamas Ministry of Foreign Affairs — eVISA online services

fee.notes: Non-refundable processing fee, in force since 18 September 2024. Apply in person to an extension officer before the time granted expires.

source.name: Bahamas Department of Immigration — Extension of Stay

passportValidity.text: Your passport must be valid for at least six months when you arrive. Passport cards are not accepted.

source.name: Bahamas Department of Immigration — Before Your Arrival

vaccinations.name: Yellow fever
vaccinations.text: A yellow fever vaccination certificate is required from travelers over one year of age arriving directly from a country with risk of yellow fever transmission, or who transited for more than 12 hours through an airport in such a country; the vaccination must have been given at least 10 days before arrival. Travelers arriving from Trinidad and Tobago are exempt.

source.name: Bahamas Department of Immigration — Before Your Arrival

travelInsurance.text: No official source we could read states a travel-insurance requirement for entry to the Bahamas. The UK government says medical treatment can be expensive, that serious cases are transferred to Nassau, Freeport or Miami by air ambulance, and advises insurance for local treatment and unexpected medical evacuation.

source.name: UK Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office — Bahamas travel advice: health

onwardTicket.text: Visitors must hold a valid return ticket or other means of leaving the Bahamas and present a completed immigration disembarkation/embarkation card at the border.

source.name: Bahamas Department of Immigration — Before Your Arrival

proofOfFunds.text: Having the financial means to support yourself for the whole stay — or naming a local sponsor who will receive you — is one of the criteria officers check at the border under the Immigration Act. No fixed amount is published.

source.name: Bahamas Department of Immigration — Before Your Arrival

declarations.name: Bahamas Immigration Disembarkation/Embarkation Card
declarations.text: Every visitor must present a completed Bahamas Immigration Disembarkation/Embarkation Card at the border interview, together with a passport valid for at least six months and a return ticket. Passengers arriving by sea also complete the Inward Passenger and Crew Manifest.

source.name: Bahamas Department of Immigration — Before Your Arrival

currencyLimits.text: Each traveller (or the responsible family member) must declare cash, negotiable instruments, precious metals or precious stones worth BSD 10,000 or more. Penalties include forfeiture of the cash and a fine of up to BSD 2,000.

source.name: Bahamas Customs Department — travellers currency declaration

Bahamas Customs Department — Arriving (USD 100 exemption; spirits, wine and tobacco allowances)

notes: Firearms and fireworks are restricted imports: Bahamas Customs allows them only with special authorization from the Commissioner of Police.

Bahamas Customs gives every visitor an exemption of $100 on dutiable articles, plus duty-free allowances for adults of one quart of spirits and one quart of wine, and one pound of tobacco or 200 cigarettes or 50 cigars. Duty and taxes apply above that.

safety.text: The UK FCDO says there have been violent crimes and armed robberies, sometimes fatal, in residential and tourist areas of New Providence and Grand Bahama, and advises not going on foot outside the main tourist areas and beaches, avoiding unlit areas and travelling in groups after dusk. It warns never to go into water that has been baited to attract marine life.

faq.question: Do I need a visa for The Bahamas?
faq.answer: Most nationalities do not. The United States, Canada, the United Kingdom and the EU are among the 155 countries, territories and islands on the Department of Immigration's visa-waiver list (as of 8 October 2026), which allows stays of up to three or eight months, as each agreement dictates. The Ministry of Foreign Affairs also lists Benin and Ghana as visa-free, but Bosnia and Herzegovina as needing a visa. If your nationality is on the visa-required list, you must obtain a Bahamian visa before traveling.

faq.question: Do US citizens need a passport for The Bahamas?
faq.answer: Yes. The Department of Immigration requires every visitor to present a passport valid for at least six months, and states that passport cards are not accepted.

faq.question: Do I have to fill in a form before arriving?
faq.answer: Yes. Every visitor presents a completed Bahamas Immigration Disembarkation/Embarkation Card at the border, and passengers arriving by sea also complete the Inward Passenger and Crew Manifest. You must also declare cash or other valuables worth BSD 10,000 or more to customs.

faq.question: How long can I stay in The Bahamas?
faq.answer: The Department of Immigration says visa waivers allow stays of up to three or eight months, as each agreement dictates, without saying which applies to which country; Canada's travel advice says Canadians may stay up to 8 months without a tourist visa. The Department can extend a visitor's stay for a non-refundable $200 processing fee if you apply before the time granted expires.

faq.question: Can I work remotely from The Bahamas?
faq.answer: No official source we could read describes a remote-work visa or permit for The Bahamas. The Department of Immigration says visitors must not intend to engage in any gainful employment while in The Bahamas.
